unit: 八下·Units 5–6 Nature's Temper / Crossing Cultures
source: 人教版八年级下册 Unit 5 Nature's Temper、Unit 6 Crossing Cultures 话题：台风、暴雨、地震等自然灾害与安全常识，不同国家的问候方式、餐桌礼仪和风俗。语言点：过去进行时（when / while）、as soon as、such ... that、be supposed to do、It's polite / impolite to do。按八年级单元测试题型编写（不含听力），百分制

items.stem: When the rainstorm came, I ______ in the library.
items.exp: 暴雨来的时候正在做某事，用过去进行时 was / were doing。

items.stem: ______ my mother was cooking dinner, my father was watching the news.
items.exp: 两个动作同时在进行，用 while 连接。

items.stem:
—What were you doing at 8 o'clock last night?
—I ______ my homework.
items.exp: 问过去某个时刻正在做什么，用过去进行时回答。

items.stem: During an earthquake, you should stay away ______ windows.
items.exp: stay away from 远离。

items.stem: The strong wind ______ many trees down last night.
items.exp: last night，用一般过去时；knock down 刮倒、撞倒。

items.stem: In China, it's polite ______ gifts with both hands.
items.exp: It's polite to do sth.，it 是形式主语。

items.stem: In some countries, you are supposed ______ your shoes before you enter a house.
items.exp: be supposed to do sth. 应该做某事（按规矩、习俗）。

items.stem: In the UK, people usually shake ______ when they meet for the first time.
items.exp: shake hands 握手，hands 用复数。

items.stem: Different countries have different customs, ______ we should respect them.
items.exp: 各国风俗不同，“所以”要尊重，用 so。

items.stem: The heavy rain ______ for three days, and the river rose quickly.
items.exp: 后半句 rose 是过去式，讲过去的事；last 持续。

items.stem: It was ______ a terrible storm that all the flights were cancelled.
items.exp: such＋a / an＋形容词＋名词＋that；so＋形容词＋that。后面是名词 storm，用 such。

items.stem: ______ the earthquake started, the students ran out of the classroom quickly and calmly.
items.exp: as soon as 一……就……。

items.stem: In Japan, people usually ______ when they greet each other.
items.exp: 日本人见面通常鞠躬 bow。

items.stem:
—Is it OK to call my Chinese teacher by her first name?
—______ We usually call teachers "Ms. + family name".
items.exp: 后面说一般称呼“老师＋姓”，所以不行：I'm afraid not。

items.stem:
—I'm going to stay with a family in France this summer.
—______ Remember to learn about their customs first.
items.exp: 对方要出行，祝旅途愉快。

sections.title: The Night of the Typhoon
sections.passage:
Last summer, I was visiting my uncle in a small town by the sea. One afternoon, while we (16) lunch, the sky suddenly became dark. The radio said a typhoon was coming. My uncle quickly (17) all the windows and moved the flower pots inside.

groups.label: A
groups.title: What to Do in an Earthquake
groups.passage:
If you are indoors: Drop to the ground, take cover under a strong table, and hold on until the shaking stops. Stay away from windows and heavy furniture. Don't use the lift.
If you are outdoors: Move to an open area away from buildings, trees and power lines.
If you are in a car: Stop the car in an open place and stay inside until the shaking stops.
After the earthquake: Check yourself and others for injuries. Be ready for aftershocks. Listen to the radio for news.

items.stem: What should you do first if you are indoors?
items.exp: Drop to the ground, take cover ... and hold on。

items.stem: What should you NOT use when you are indoors?
options: The stairs after the shaking stops.
items.exp: Don't use the lift。

items.stem: Where should you go if you are outdoors?
items.exp: Move to an open area away from buildings, trees and power lines。

options: Stop in an open place and stay inside the car.
items.exp: Stop the car in an open place and stay inside until the shaking stops。

items.stem: Why should people listen to the radio after an earthquake?
items.exp: Listen to the radio for news。

groups.label: B
groups.title: Table Manners Around the World
groups.passage:
Table manners are different around the world. If you are invited to dinner in another country, it's a good idea to learn about them first.
In China, don't stick your chopsticks straight up in a bowl of rice. Many people think it brings bad luck. It's also polite to let older people start eating first.
In Japan, it's OK to make noise when you eat noodles. In fact, it shows that you are enjoying the food!
In India, many people eat with their hands. But remember to use your right hand only.
In Korea, you shouldn't start eating before the oldest person at the table does. And you are supposed to leave your rice bowl on the table, not pick it up.
Don't worry if you make a mistake. Most people will understand. The most important thing is to show respect.

items.stem: Why shouldn't you stick your chopsticks straight up in rice in China?
options: Because the rice will get cold.
Because many people think it brings bad luck.
items.exp: Many people think it brings bad luck。

items.stem: What does making noise when eating noodles in Japan show?
items.exp: it shows that you are enjoying the food。

items.stem: Which hand should you use to eat in India?
items.exp: remember to use your right hand only。

items.stem: In which country are you supposed to leave your rice bowl on the table?
items.exp: In Korea ... leave your rice bowl on the table, not pick it up。

items.stem: What is the most important thing according to the writer?
items.exp: The most important thing is to show respect。

sections.title: Emma's Month in China
sections.passage:
Last year, Emma, an exchange student from Canada, stayed with my family for a month. On her first evening, while we (36) (have) dinner, she stuck her chopsticks straight up in her rice. My grandma looked (37) (surprise). I (38) (quick) explained the Chinese custom to Emma, and she said sorry at once.
After that, Emma became very interested in Chinese (39) (custom). She asked me (40) (teach) her how to use chopsticks properly. She also learned (41) (say) "Happy New Year" in Chinese.
One day, it was raining heavily when we (42) (walk) home from school. Emma told me that in Canada, people often (43) (talk) about the weather when they meet. "It's (44) ______ easy way to start a conversation," she said.
I learned a lot from Emma. Understanding different cultures helps us become (45) (good) friends.

items.exp: while 引导正在进行的动作，主语 we，用 were having。
look 是系动词，人感到惊讶用 surprised。
修饰动词 explained 用副词 quickly。
泛指中国的各种风俗，用复数 customs。
ask sb. to do sth. 请某人做某事。
learn to do sth. 学做某事。
下大雨的时候我们正在走路回家，用过去进行时。
说的是加拿大人平时的习惯，用一般现在时，主语 people 用原形。
easy 以元音音素开头，用 an；a way 表示“一种方法”。
become better friends 成为更好的朋友，用比较级。

sections.prompt:
你的英国笔友 Lucy 下个月来中国，到你家做客。请给她写一封信：1. 欢迎她来；2. 介绍中国家庭聚餐的礼仪，至少三条（可用 be supposed to / It's polite to / You shouldn't）；3. 告诉她不用太紧张。要求：80 词左右，开头和结尾已给出，不计入总词数；文中不得出现真实姓名和校名。
Dear Lucy,
……
Yours,
Li Hua
points: 介绍至少三条餐桌礼仪
语言正确（be supposed to do、It's polite to do、shouldn't），书写规范
sections.sample:
Dear Lucy,
I'm so happy that you're coming to China next month! My family and I are looking forward to having dinner with you.
Here are some Chinese table manners. First, you're supposed to wait until the older people start eating. Second, it's polite to try a little of every dish, and you can say "It's delicious!" to the cook. Third, you shouldn't stick your chopsticks straight up in your rice, because many people think it brings bad luck. Also, when someone gives you something, it's polite to take it with both hands.
Don't be nervous. My family will understand if you make a mistake. See you soon!
Yours,
Li Hua
sections.exp: 写完检查：be supposed to、It's polite to 后接动词原形；礼仪要给出理由或说明，读起来才像真的在介绍；结尾安慰对方，语气要友好。
